title: Did you know… Ishmael was also given promises, not just Isaac?
paragraphs: Did you know… Ishmael was also given promises, not just Isaac?
He wasn’t the chosen son…
But he was still seen by God.
Ishmael.
The boy most people reduce to a footnote—“the other son.” The mistake. The detour. The consequence of Abraham and Sarah’s impatience.
But heaven didn’t call him a mistake.

Genesis tells us something raw, something almost scandalous:
God made promises to Ishmael too.
Not just Isaac.
Not just the “child of promise.”

Ishmael cried in the wilderness…
abandoned, thirsty, unwanted.
And God showed up.

Not for the perfect plan—
but for the broken situation.
“And God heard the voice of the boy…” (Genesis 21:17)
Heard him.

In the desert.
In rejection.
In the aftermath of someone else’s poor decision.
And here’s what hits hard—

God didn’t just rescue Ishmael.
He blessed him. Multiplied him. Gave him a future.
But here’s what we must not miss…
Blessing is not the same as covenant.

Ishmael received provision.
Isaac carried the promise.

Through Isaac would come the lineage—
and ultimately, Jesus Christ.
That’s the Gospel thread.
Because this isn’t just about two sons.
It’s about two ways of living:

• One born of human striving
• One born of divine promise

Galatians 4 breaks it open—
Ishmael represents the flesh.
Isaac represents the Spirit.

One is effort.
The other is grace.
And if we’re honest?

We’ve all lived like Ishmael at some point—
trying to force outcomes…
fix timelines…
earn what can only be received.
But here’s where grace walks in.

Even when you’ve created Ishmael moments—
God still sees you.
Still hears you.
Still provides.
But He doesn’t stop there.

He invites you higher—
not just into blessing…
…but into promise fulfilled in Christ.
Because through Jesus, you’re not the “other son.”
You are brought into the family of promise.

Chosen.
Redeemed.
Adopted.

Not by effort—
but by grace alone.
So if you’ve been living in the wilderness of your own decisions…
Hear this:

God hasn’t abandoned you.
But He’s calling you out of survival—into surrender.
From striving—into salvation.
From Ishmael… to Isaac.
And it’s only possible through Jesus.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
